landmarks.name: Le Morne Brabant
landmarks.writeup: A UNESCO World Heritage site, this mountain is a symbol of resistance against slavery.

wiki.extract: Le Morne Brabant is a peninsula at the extreme southwestern tip of the Indian Ocean island of Mauritius. On it is a basaltic monolith of the same name 556 metres high. Its summit covers an area of over 12 hectares. There are many caves and overhangs on the steep slopes. It is largely surrounded by a lagoon and is a well known tourist attraction. It is also a refuge for two rare plants, the Mandrinette and the Boucle d'Oreille. The peninsula of Le Morne benefits from a micro-climate. The mountain is named after the Dutch East India Company ship Brabant that ran aground here on 29 December 1783.

landmarks.name: Black River Gorges National Park
landmarks.writeup: A large national park known for its biodiversity and hiking trails.

wiki.extract: Black River Gorges National Park is a national park located in the mountainous south-western region of Mauritius. It is the largest protected area on the island and was officially proclaimed on 15 June 1994. The park is managed by the National Parks and Conservation Service (Mauritius) and plays an important role in protecting the remaining native forests and endangered species of Mauritius.

landmarks.name: Aapravasi Ghat
landmarks.writeup: A historic site where indentured laborers first arrived, now a UNESCO World Heritage site.

wiki.extract: Aapravasi Ghat is a building complex located in Port Louis, Mauritius, the first British colony to receive indentured, or contracted, labour workforce from many countries. From 1849 to 1923, half a million Indian indentured labourers passed through the Immigration Depot, to be transported to plantations throughout the British Empire. The large-scale migration of the labourers left an indelible mark on the societies of many former British colonies, with Indians constituting a substantial proportion of their national populations. In Mauritius alone, 68 percent of the current total population is of Indian ancestry. The Immigration Depot has thus become an important reference point in the history and cultural identity of Mauritius.

landmarks.name: Chamarel Seven Colored Earths
landmarks.writeup: A natural phenomenon featuring sand dunes with seven distinct colors.

wiki.extract: The Seven Coloured Earths are a geological formation and prominent tourist attraction found in the Chamarel plain of the Rivière Noire District in south-western Mauritius. It is a relatively small area of sand dunes comprising sand of seven distinct colours. The main feature of the place is that since these differently coloured sands spontaneously settle in different layers, dunes acquire a surrealistic, striped colouring. Since the earth was first exposed, rains have carved beautiful patterns into the hillside, creating an effect of earthen meringue.

landmarks.name: Pamplemousses Botanical Garden
landmarks.writeup: One of the oldest botanical gardens in the Southern Hemisphere, famous for giant water lilies.

wiki.extract: The Sir Seewoosagur Ramgoolam Botanic Garden, commonly known as the Pamplemousses Botanic Garden, is a popular tourist attraction in Pamplemousses, near Port Louis, Mauritius, and the oldest botanical garden in the Southern Hemisphere. Famous for its long pond of giant water lilies, the garden, first constructed by Pierre Poivre in 1770, covers an area of around 37 hectares.

cultural_events.name: Cavadee Festival
cultural_events.writeup: A Tamil Hindu festival marked by acts of devotion and colorful processions.

wiki.extract: Kavadi Aattam is a ceremonial sacrifice and offering practiced by devotees during the worship of Murugan, the Hindu god of war. It is a central part of the festival of Thaipusam and emphasizes debt bondage. The Kavadi ("burden") itself is a physical burden, the bearing of which is used by the devotee to implore Murugan for assistance, usually on behalf of a loved one who is in need of healing, or as a means of balancing a spiritual debt. Devotees process and dance along a pilgrimage route while bearing these burdens.

cultural_events.name: Diwali
cultural_events.writeup: The Hindu festival of lights celebrated with fireworks and family gatherings.

wiki.extract: Dipavali, commonly known as Diwali, is the Hindu festival of lights, with variations celebrated in other Indian religions such as Jainism and Sikhism. It symbolises the spiritual victory of Dharma over Adharma, light over darkness, good over evil, and knowledge over ignorance. Diwali is celebrated during the Hindu lunisolar months of Ashvin and Kārtika – between around mid-October and mid-November. The celebrations generally last five or six days.

cultural_events.name: Chinese Spring Festival
cultural_events.writeup: Celebration of the Lunar New Year with traditional dances and food.

wiki.extract: Chinese New Year, also known as the Spring Festival, marks the beginning of a new year on the traditional lunisolar Chinese calendar. It is one of the most important holidays in Chinese culture. Marking the end of winter and the beginning of spring, this festival takes place from Chinese New Year's Eve to the Lantern Festival, held on the 15th day of the year. The first day of the Chinese New Year falls on the new moon that appears between 21 January and 20 February.

cultural_events.name: Mauritius Carnival
cultural_events.writeup: An annual event featuring music, dance, and vibrant costumes.

wiki.extract: Carnival is a festive season at the close of the Christian pre-Lenten period, consisting of Quinquagesima or Shrove Sunday, Shrove Monday, and Shrove Tuesday or Mardi Gras.

food_writeup: Mauritian cuisine is a blend of Creole, Indian, Chinese, and French influences, featuring dishes like dholl puri, fish vindaye, and gateau piment.
brief_history: Mauritius was uninhabited until the Dutch arrived in the 17th century. It was colonized by the French and later the British before gaining independence in 1968. The island has a diverse cultural heritage influenced by African, Indian, European, and Chinese settlers.

commentary.inflation_management: The Bank of Mauritius operates a managed float with price stability as the objective, and its record is solid. Inflation peaked at 10.8% in 2022, the series high, during the global commodity shock, and troughed at 0.5% in 2019. It ran at 8-10% in 2006-2008 on food and energy prices, then settled into a 1-7% range for a decade. The bank hiked rates in 2022-23 to contain the shock, bringing inflation down to 3.6% in 2024 and a projected 3.7% in 2025. The framework is credible and the bank is well-regarded; the main vulnerability is imported inflation, which no domestic policy can prevent in an island economy.
commentary.debt_management: Mauritius entered the period with already-high debt (54.6% of GDP in 2006) and has never brought it down durably. It fell to 48.8% in 2007, the series low, then climbed through the 2010s as governments borrowed for infrastructure and social spending: 81.3% by 2019. COVID's tourism collapse drove it to 91.9% in 2020, the series high, and it remains elevated at a projected 85.9% in 2025 despite the tourism rebound. The debt is mostly domestic and the financial system is sophisticated, which has kept servicing feasible, but at 86% of GDP for a small island economy, the buffer for the next shock is thin, and IMF assessments consistently urge consolidation.

key_events.event: Global financial crisis hit textiles and tourism; stimulus raised debt.
Political transition; economic diversification into finance and ICT continued.
COVID-19 shut down tourism; debt hit 91.9% of GDP, the series high.
Ukraine war pushed inflation to 10.8%; tourism recovery began.
November 2024: Navin Ramgoolam's Alliance du Changement swept the election, ending the Jugnauth era.

commentary.outlook_next_decade: The base case is continued tourism and financial-services growth with inflation near 3-4% and debt slowly declining if the new government consolidates. Upside comes from diversification and African financial hub ambitions; downside is debt: at 86% of GDP, another tourism shock would force painful adjustment. Uncertainty is moderate: institutions are strong and the 2024 transition was democratic, but fiscal consolidation has been promised by every government and delivered by none.
commentary.caveat: Outlook is an analytical assessment as of October 2026, not a forecast. 2025 figures are IMF estimates/projections.
